Subject: Follow-up: Access controls & support access (FinTrust)

Tom — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can map Redwood's controls to FinTrust requirements: 

Summary from call:
- FinTrust needs clear RBAC model across API, Console, and support tools. Primary roles: Admin, Engineering (limited), Billing, Support (read-only except break-glass).
- Least-privilege: long-lived keys should be scoped; JIT/temporary elevation preferred.
- Support access: must be auditable, require approval, and limited to specific incidents (break-glass).
- Data residency: production data must remain in EU regions.
- Logging & retention: access logs retained for at least 12 months; audit trails required for support activity.

Attachments: SOC2-summary.pdf (high-level), redwood-support-access-policy.pdf (support process).

Request from FinTrust: can you confirm the exact retention windows you need for logs and whether you expect support sessions to require customer approval before elevation? Also please attach any internal access matrix you have (roles -> allowed actions).

Next steps: 
1) Tom: send access matrix / required retention (if you can attach by Friday).
2) Rishi (SE): will prepare a short doc mapping Redwood roles to your matrix and propose config options.
3) Security sync: Soojin will follow up with evidence / options for audited break-glass.

Let me know if I missed anything. Happy to jump on a 20-min follow-up next week if useful.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Appreciate the matrix and the clarifications, Tom. High-level responses below — I'll have Rishi produce a mapping doc that references specific Console/API settings and roles.

1) RBAC & least-privilege:
- Redwood supports role-based roles that map to your matrix (Admin, Developer, Billing, Support). Roles can be scoped by project/environment and by model.
- Long-lived API keys can be scoped to read-only or read-write; we recommend using short-lived keys for high-privilege operations. We support OAuth-based tokens and integration with customer identity providers (SAML/OIDC) for SSO + SCIM provisioning.

2) Support & break-glass:
- Support engineers have a distinct "Support" role with no default write permissions. Break-glass is implemented as a time-limited elevation (JIT) that requires: a ticket reference, approval from a configured approver group (your on-call security), and is logged as an auditable event.
- Every break-glass event logs the actor, approver, reason, duration, and an exported record (JSON) which can be pushed to your SIEM. We can also trigger email notifications to a configured mailbox.

3) Logging & retention:
- Access logs, admin audit trails, and support elevation logs are configurable; default retention is 12 months, but we support configurable retention windows up to 36 months. We can set your workspace to 13 months to match your policy.

4) Data residency:
- We can pin workloads to EU regions (Frankfurt or Amsterdam). Persisted artifacts, model inputs, and logs for pinned workspaces will remain in-region.

5) Evidence & compliance docs:
- Soojin (cc) will share SOC 2 artifacts and can scope the evidence package for an on-site or virtual review.

I'll loop Rishi to produce the mapping doc and propose a short demo focused on: RBAC model, support elevation workflow, and audit/export options.

Thanks —
Marissa
